result.instructions: Use the typed agent_browser_* tools to control a browser. Active MCP tools profile(s): core. Prefer agent_browser_snapshot after navigation to obtain stable element refs before clicking or typing. When a navigation result lists saved flows that match the task, call agent_browser_flow_run instead of driving the page. Use agent_browser_tools_profiles to see available startup profiles. Every tool accepts these optional arguments even when its schema does not list them: session (isolated browser session name), restore (true or a key; restores and auto-saves browser state when the call launches the browser), allowedDomains (domain patterns that restrict browser and read traffic when the call launches the browser; also disables RTCPeerConnection in Chromium sessions, and is rejected when the server environment or config already sets allowed domains), capture (set to flow to record the session so flow steps and flow save can turn it into a reusable flow, when the call launches the browser), extraArgs (extra CLI arguments such as --engine; global flags that change network, file, policy, or host access, such as --allowed-domains, --executable-path, --args, and --config, are rejected, so set those in the MCP server environment or config), timeoutMs (positive integer, maximum milliseconds to wait for the tool call), namespace (isolates daemon sockets and restore-state directories), restoreSave (auto, always, or never), restoreCheckUrl, restoreCheckText, and restoreCheckFn (conditions restored state must satisfy), caCert (path to a CA certificate or PEM bundle for the CLI's HTTPS requests and locally launched Chromium on Linux), useSystemCa (boolean, use the OS trust store for the CLI's HTTPS requests), clearCaCert (boolean, clear CA trust retained by the session; cannot be combined with caCert), idleTimeout (such as 30s, 5m, 1h, or milliseconds; defaults to 1h, 0 disables idle shutdown), and relaunch (boolean, relaunch the session's browser even when no setting changed).

tools.description: Launch the browser and optionally navigate to a URL. On macOS, installed browsers are searched in /Applications, then ~/Applications. Set the proxy in the server environment or config; percent-encoded proxy URL credentials are decoded before authentication. On Windows, owned headless Chrome uses a private desktop and its process tree closes with the daemon, including forced termination. Headed browsers use the interactive desktop. Successful navigation responses include WebMCP availability metadata when the page exposes allowed tools. Browser-provider and launch-mutation errors omit response error text and unsupported protocol values.

tools.name: sandbox.diagnostics
tools.description: One-shot Kitesurf plugin diagnostics: engine status, phase, targets, settings, console tail, operation trace, errorId catalogue and generated next-step hints. Call this FIRST when anything fails.

tools.name: sandbox.console
tools.description: Recent page console/error/exception/network/navigation events captured over the plugin CDP socket.Levels: log,info,warn,error,exception,network,navigation.

tools.name: sandbox.operations
tools.description: Recent /nano-local-sandbox/* route calls with status, errorId, incidentId, durationMs and a whitelisted input summary. Use errorsOnly=true to see only failures.

tools.name: sandbox.error_catalog
tools.description: The single source of truth: errorId → HTTP status → cause → next command. Use it to interpret any kitesurf.* errorId instead of guessing.

tools.name: sandbox.targets
tools.description: Engine CDP Target.getTargets result: page target ids/urls and which page the plugin socket is attached to. Use when the pane and the API disagree.

tools.name: sandbox.history
tools.description: Browse history for the Kitesurf pane: the newest 30 visits with url, ISO time and visit count, plus the total stored. Backed by the plugin durable store (the Kitesurf workerd exposes no D1/KV binding). Mutations go through the host: DELETE /nano-local-sandbox/browse-history?id=… or POST {clear:true}.

tools.name: sandbox.dom
tools.description: Last captured document: url, byte size and the first 4000 characters of documentElement.outerHTML. Use to confirm what the engine is actually rendering when the pane looks wrong.

tools.name: sandbox.elements
tools.description: Elements panel data from the Kitesurf DOM/CSS domains: the last DOM tree (up to 40 nodes with tag/id/class/child count), the selector queried, and how many computed properties were returned. Call GET /nano-local-sandbox/elements?selector=… on the host for styles of a specific node.

tools.name: sandbox.snapshot
tools.description: a11y-lite snapshot: the last semantic tree + @N element-ref table the host pushed. Refs (@1..@N) resolve via GET /nano-local-sandbox/refs?ref=@N or are accepted directly in wait/pick/evaluate/edit selector fields on the host. This is the shared language between a human pick and an agent action. For a live re-walk call GET /nano-local-sandbox/snapshot on the authenticated host.

tools.name: sandbox.control
tools.description: Page control/ownership state: which writer holds the page (owner client name, since when, last write). One page is shared by a human and agents; a second writer is refused kitesurf.control.busy rather than tearing navigation. action: status|claim|release — claim to take the page, release to free it.

tools.name: sandbox.selftest
tools.description: One verdict over every layer: plugin build, engine identity, container state, published port loopback, MCP bridge counters, CDP targets, DOM availability, route table and phase consistency. Use after any restart or container change.

tools.name: sandbox.network
tools.description: Network waterfall from the Kitesurf CDP session: method, url, status, mimeType, bytes and duration for every request. failedOnly=true shows 4xx/5xx and transport failures only.

tools.name: sandbox.ports
tools.description: Port truth: what the profile configured, what the engine actually uses, what the container published, and whether each host port is free (e.g. 8787 held by Cursor while the engine runs on 8798). Read this FIRST for any container/bootstrap failure.

tools.name: sandbox.recovery_plan
tools.description: Ordered recovery steps with the exact HTTP call for each, derived from the live snapshot (port conflict, engine down, phase mismatch, container missing). Returns commands to run through the authenticated host session.

tools.name: sandbox.bridge_health
tools.description: MCP bridge liveness: conns, accepted, rejected, uptimeMs and when the last host diagnostics snapshot was pushed.
